source_text: Item legit: Quid enim dubitemus redemptori nostro sacrificium istius humilitatis offerre? an uero ille de caelis in membra descendit humana, ut membra eius essemus, et nos, ne ipsa eius membra crudeli diuisione lanientur, de cathedris descendere formidamus? propter nos nihil sufficientius quam christiani fideles et oboedientes sumus; hoc ergo semper simus. episcopi autem propter christianos populos ordinamur; quod ergo christianis populis ad christianam pacem prodest, hoc de nostro episcopatu faciamus. Augustinus episcopus dixit: Propter nos hoc debemus esse quod uos. quid debes esse tu cuicumque loquor uestrum? christianus fidelis oboediens. hoc tu propter te, hoc et ego propter me. ergo, quod tu propter te et ego propter me, semper esse debemus, quod autem sum propter te, sim si tibi prodest, non sim si tibi obest. ecce quod dictum est attendite. item legit: Si serui utiles sumus, cur domini aeternis lucris pro nostris temporalibus sublimitatibus inuidemus? episcopalis dignitas fructuosior nobis erit, si gregem Christi deposita magis collegerit quam retenta disperserit. cumque recitaret, Augustinus episcopus dixit: Fratres mei, si dominum cogitamus, locus iste altior specula uinitoris est, non fastigium superbientis. si, cum uolo retinere episcopatum meum, dispergo gregem Christi, quomodo est damnum gregis honor pastoris? item legit: Nam qua fronte in futuro saeculo promissum a Christo sperabimus honorem, si christianam in hoc saeculo noster honor impedit unitatem? haec propterea praelostantiae tuae scribenda curauimus et ut per innotescant omnibus postulamus, ut in adiutorio domini dei nostri, quo admonente ista promittimus et quo adiuuante nos implere posse confidimus, etiam ante collationem, si fieri potest, corda hominum uel infirma uel dura pia caritas aut sanet aut edomet ac sic iam pacificis mentibus non resistamus manifestissimae ueritati et disputationem uel praecedamus concordia uel sequamur. neque enim desperare debemus, si recolunt esse pacificos beatos, quoniam ipsi filii dei uocabun- . tur, multo dignius et facilius eos uelle, ut pars Donati uniuerso orbi christiano reconcilietur quam uniuersus orbis christianus a parte Donati rebaptizetur, cum praesertim de Maximiani sacrilego e t damnato schismate uenientes, quos etiam terrenarum potestatum iussionibus insectando emendare curarunt, tanta diligentia quaesierunt, ut nec baptismum ab eis datum rescindere auderent et quosdam eorum damnatos sine ulla honoris diminutione susciperent, quosdam uero in illius discissionis societate impollutos esse censerent. quorum inter se concordiae non inuidemus, sed eos oportet aduertere, quam pie ramum a se fractum tanto studio radix catholica inquirit, si ramus ipse similiter a se paruum fragmen incisum sic colligere laborauit. et alia manu: optamus te, fili, in domino bene ualere.
thought_title: Bishops should lay down their rank for the flock's peace
orientation: Alypius is reading aloud the Catholic bishops' letter from the Council of Zerta, and Augustine interrupts to explain its point about laying down the bishopric for the people's good.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise he read: Why indeed should we hesitate to offer to our redeemer the sacrifice of this humility? or truly did he descend from the heavens into human members, so that we might be his members, and we, lest his very members be torn by cruel division, do we fear to descend from chairs? for ourselves nothing [is] more sufficient than [that] we are faithful and obedient Christians; this therefore let us always be. bishops however are ordained for the sake of Christian peoples; what therefore is useful to Christian peoples for Christian peace, this let us do concerning our episcopate. Augustine the bishop said: For ourselves we ought to be this which you [are]. what ought you to be, you to whomever of you I speak? a faithful obedient Christian. this you for yourself, this also I for myself. therefore, what you for yourself and I for myself, we ought always to be, but what I am for you, may I be if it is useful to you, may I not be if it is harmful to you. behold what has been said, attend. Likewise he read: If we are useful servants, why do we envy the Lord's eternal gains for our temporal heights? episcopal dignity will be more fruitful to us, if it gathers the flock of Christ more by being laid down than disperses [it] by being retained. and while he was reading, Augustine the bishop said: My brothers, if we consider the Lord, this higher place is a watchtower of a vine-dresser, not a summit of one being proud. if, when I wish to retain my episcopate, I scatter the flock of Christ, how is the loss of the flock the honor of the shepherd? Likewise he read: For with what face shall we hope for the honor promised by Christ in the future age, if our honor hinders Christian unity in this age? these things for this reason we have taken care to write to your pre-eminence and we ask that they be made known to all, so that in the help of the Lord our God, by whom admonishing we promise these things and by whom helping we trust that we are able to fulfill [them], even before the conference, if it can happen, pious love may either heal or tame the hearts of men either weak or hard and thus now with pacified minds we may not resist the most manifest truth and may either precede the disputation with concord or follow [it]. for neither ought we to despair, if they recall that the peaceful [are] blessed, since they themselves will be called sons of God, [that] much more worthily and easily they wish that the party of Donatus be reconciled to the whole Christian world than the whole Christian world be rebaptized by the party of Donatus, since especially those coming from the sacrilegious and condemned schism of Maximian, whom also by the commands of earthly powers by pursuing they took care to correct, with so great diligence they sought, that they did not dare to rescind the baptism given by them and some of them condemned they received without any diminution of honor, but some they judged to be unpolluted in the society of that division. whose concord among themselves we do not envy, but it is fitting for them to notice, how piously the catholic root seeks with so great zeal a branch broken from itself, if the branch itself similarly labored to gather a small fragment cut from itself. and in another hand: we desire you, son, to fare well in the Lord.

choices.why: Keeps the literal image of the bishop's seat, matching the source's concrete 'cathedris' rather than abstracting to 'office'.
rejected: to step down from our thrones

choices.why: Preserves the three-word asyndeton and the exact word order of the source, which Augustine repeats for emphasis.
rejected: a Christian who is faithful and obedient

choices.why: Renders the agricultural image literally; 'uinitor' is specifically a vine-dresser, tying to the vine imagery of John 15.
Keeps the architectural contrast with 'watchtower' and the active participle 'superbientis' as 'proud man's'.
The source has an unusual form 'praelostantiae' (likely for 'praestantiae'); rendering as 'eminence' preserves the formal address to Marcellinus.
Keeps the passive participle 'fractum' and the reflexive 'a se' to show the branch broke itself off from the root.

bible_refs.note: beati pacifici, quoniam filii dei uocabuntur

pass_b_english: Why should we hesitate to offer our Redeemer the sacrifice of this humility? Did he descend from heaven into human limbs so that we might be his limbs, and do we fear to descend from our chairs so that those very limbs of his may not be torn apart by a cruel division? For ourselves, nothing is more fitting than to be faithful obedient Christians; so let us always be that. But bishops are ordained for the sake of Christian peoples; so whatever benefits Christian peoples for Christian peace, let us do that with our bishopric.

Augustine the bishop said: For your sakes we ought to be what you are. What ought you to be—you, whoever I am speaking to among you? A faithful obedient Christian. That you are for yourself, and that I am for myself. So what you are for yourself and I am for myself, we ought always to be; but what I am for your sake, let me be if it benefits you, and not be if it harms you. Pay attention to what has been said.

He read on: If we are useful servants, why do we begrudge the Lord eternal gains for the sake of our temporal heights? The dignity of a bishop will be more fruitful for us if, laid down, it gathers the flock of Christ rather than, kept, it scatters them. And while he was reading, Augustine the bishop said: My brothers, if we think of the Lord, this higher place is a vinedresser's watchtower, not a proud man's pinnacle. If, when I want to keep my bishopric, I scatter the flock of Christ, how is the loss of the flock the honor of the shepherd?

He read on: For with what face shall we hope for the honor promised by Christ in the age to come, if our honor in this age hinders Christian unity? We have taken care to write these things to your eminence, and we ask that they be made known to all, so that with the help of the Lord our God—by whose admonition we promise these things and by whose aid we trust we can fulfill them—even before the conference, if it can happen, loving charity may either heal or subdue the weak or hard hearts of men, and so with minds already at peace we may not resist the most manifest truth, and may either precede the debate with concord or follow it. For we ought not to despair, if we recall that the peacemakers are blessed, for they shall be called sons of God (Matthew 5:9), that it is much more worthy and easy for them to want the Donatist party to be reconciled to the whole Christian world than for the whole Christian world to be rebaptized by the Donatist party—especially since, in the case of those coming from the sacrilegious and condemned schism of Maximianus, whom they even took care to correct by pursuing them with the orders of earthly powers, they sought them with such great diligence that they did not dare to invalidate the baptism given by them, and they received some of them who had been condemned without any diminution of honor, while they judged others to be unpolluted in the fellowship of that division. We do not begrudge their concord among themselves, but they ought to notice how devoutly the Catholic root seeks the branch broken from itself with such great effort, if the branch itself likewise labored to gather a small fragment cut from itself. And in another hand: We desire that you be well in the Lord, son.
notes: The source has 'praelostantiae' where classical Latin would have 'praestantiae'; this is likely a scribal variant or error, but the text is legible and translated as 'your eminence'.

The phrase 'et alia manu' indicates a change of handwriting in the manuscript, not a change of speaker; the closing greeting 'optamus te, fili, in domino bene ualere' is part of the letter being read.

problems.why: "Recolunt" means "if we recall/remember" (the bishops speaking of themselves), not "if they recall." The subject is the bishops writing the letter, not some third party. This changes agency and speaker.

problems.quote: that they would much more worthily and easily want the Donatist party to be reconciled to the whole Christian world than the whole Christian world to be rebaptized by the Donatist party
problems.source_quote: multo dignius et facilius eos uelle, ut pars Donati uniuerso orbi christiano reconcilietur quam uniuersus orbis christianus a parte Donati rebaptizetur
problems.why: 'eos' refers to the Donatists; it's more fitting for them to seek reconciliation than to rebaptize the world.
problems.fix: that it is much more worthy and easy for them to want the Donatist party to be reconciled to the whole Christian world than for the whole Christian world to be rebaptized by the Donatist party
problems.ruling: 'eos' refers to the Donatists (not 'they' as peacemakers generally); 'dignius et facilius' modifies what the Donatists should want, not what 'we' want.

problems.quote: for the sake of Catholic peace
problems.why: The Latin says "to/for Christian peace," not "for the sake of Catholic peace." This changes the specific claim and misapplies the glossary term.
problems.ruling: Source says "ad christianam pacem" (Christian peace), not "Catholic peace"; changes the specific wording.

problems.quote: For ourselves we ought to be what you are
problems.source_quote: Propter nos hoc debemus esse quod uos
problems.why: Augustine addresses the bishops' statement and turns it to the people: "For your sakes we ought to be what you are" (i.e., bishops should be what the people are—Christians). "For ourselves" inverts the meaning.
problems.fix: For your sakes we ought to be what you are
problems.ruling: "Propter nos" = "for our/your sakes"; "for ourselves" inverts Augustine's meaning that bishops exist for the people.

fixed: si recolunt: subject is the bishops writing the letter, so 'we recall' is correct.
multo dignius et facilius eos uelle: 'eos' refers to the Donatists; the construction is 'it is more worthy and easy for them to want...'
ad christianam pacem: the Latin says 'Christian peace,' not 'Catholic peace.'
Propter nos hoc debemus esse quod uos: Augustine turns the bishops' statement to the people, so 'For your sakes' is correct.

problems.source_quote: si recolunt esse pacificos beatos, quoniam ipsi filii dei uocabuntur
problems.why: Source reads 'si recolunt' (if they recall), third person plural referring to the Donatists, not 'we recall.' Speaker shifts to the Donatists' own reasoning.
problems.fix: if they recall that the peacemakers are blessed, for they shall be called sons of God (Matthew 5:9)
problems.ruling: 'si recolunt' = 'if they [Donatists] recall,' not 'we recall'; subject misidentified, misattributing reasoning.

problems.why: The subject of "recolunt" is "they" (the Donatists, implied from context), not "we." The bishops are saying the Donatists should recall this, not that the bishops themselves recall it.
problems.ruling: "si recolunt" = "if they recall" (Donatists), not "if we recall"; wrong subject changes meaning.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'uinator' = vintner/wine-taster, not vinedresser; different role.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Vinitor' from 'vitis' = vine; 'vinedresser' is standard meaning (OLD: vine-dresser, vine-grower). 'Vintner' is wrong.

last_rejected.ruling: 'Item legit' = 'he read on'; third-person narrative voice is preserved. No meaning lost; mere preference for naming Alypius.

last_rejected.ruling: 'alia manu' = 'another hand'; refers to handwriting style, not reader. Translation is accurate; no voice obscured.

last_rejected.source_quote: pia caritas aut sanet aut edomet
last_rejected.why: 'Loving charity' is tautological and weakens 'pia' (devout/pious); 'charity' alone suffices.
last_rejected.fix: devout charity may either heal or subdue
last_rejected.ruling: 'pia caritas' = 'loving charity' is within normal range; 'pia' = pious/loving. Mere preference, not error.

last_rejected.quote: they even took care to correct by pursuing them with the orders of earthly powers
last_rejected.source_quote: quos etiam terrenarum potestatum iussionibus insectando emendare curarunt
last_rejected.why: 'Correct' is too mild for 'emendare' here; 'took care to correct' obscures that they hunted them down.
last_rejected.fix: whom they even took care to reform by hounding them with earthly powers' orders
last_rejected.ruling: 'emendare' = correct/amend; 'insectando' = pursuing, already rendered. 'Correct' is valid; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: they sought them with such great diligence
last_rejected.why: 'Sought' is ambiguous; 'quaesierunt' here means they demanded/inquired after them (legally).
last_rejected.fix: they demanded them with such great diligence
last_rejected.ruling: 'quaesierunt' = sought; standard meaning. 'Demanded' is a preference; 'sought' is accurate and not misleading.
